correctness.rationale: The proof folds the 2n-vertex cubic Möbius ladder into n antipodal columns; every uniform column contributes one bad chord, mixed interfaces one bad cycle edge, and matched split-split links zero or two with a twisted seam. At even n>=4 the all-split parity obstruction gives minimum two defects, exactly 2n ground states; a single uniform column produces the 4n states at three defects and exactly two neighboring grounds each, with each ground connected to four such intermediates. Swapping a chord pair moves the sole defective link; one n-step circuit produces spin reversal and the 2n ground graph is a cycle with every edge doubled by two length-two paths. For odd n>=3 the graph is bipartite: states correspond to flipped subsets S and u(s)=|delta(S)|. The folded boundary classification identifies exactly two 0-defect states, 4n three-defect states, n(n+3) four-defect states, two connected B_n components and n(n-3) isolated 4-defect states. Sequentially flipping complete antipodal columns achieves at most five defects between the two grounds, and level-four disconnection proves sharpness. Independent exhaustive direct enumeration of all 2^(2n) spin configurations at n=3,4,5,6,7 reproduced all levels/component counts and even 2n-cycle doubled two-step adjacency. The graph geometry for every n follows from the parity/cut proof rather than the finite scan.

value.rationale: The antiferromagnetic Möbius ladder is a canonical frustrated cubic spin graph. Its low-energy single-spin transition network is an intrinsic dynamical invariant important for barriers and metastability, unlike merely determining ground-state degeneracy or cutwidth. The result supplies an exact topological graph description with isolated traps at a natural energy cutoff and a sharp communication barrier. The odd-even parity switch gives a meaningful structural phase split and a complete natural finite-energy window without requiring a general dynamics theorem.
